Στίχ. κεʹ. ∆ιεξέλθοι δὲ διὰ σώματος αὐτοῦ βέλος. Τὰ βέλη ταῦτα τὰ πεπυρωμένα
τιτρώσκει αὐτόν. Στίχ. κεʹ. Κατέδεται αὐτὸν πῦρ ἄκαυστον. Μυστήριόν τι
μανθάνομεν περὶ τῆς κολάσεως τῆς ἀποκειμένης, ἵνα φυλασσώμεθα αὐτὴν παθεῖν.
Πῦρ εἶπεν ἄκαυστον κατέδεσθαι τὸν ἀσεβῆ· τοῦτο τὸ πῦρ τὸ παρ' ἡμῖν ὑλικὸν οὐκ
ἔστιν ἄκαυστον πῦρ· βλεπό μενον γὰρ αὐτό. Ἐκεῖνο δὲ ἀόρατόν ἐστι τὸ πῦρ, τὸ ἐπὶ
τοὺς ἁμαρτωλοὺς ἐρχόμενον, ὃ ἔνδον αὐτοὺς καίει. Νοητόν ἐστι καὶ κολάζον. Ἐὰν
θέλῃς εἰκόνα παραλαβεῖν ἐκείνου τοῦ πυρὸς, νόει μοι τὸν εἰς ὑπερβολὴν
πυρέσσοντα, καὶ ὑπὸ πυρὸς φλεγόμενον. Οὐχ εὑρή σεις ὄψει τὸ πῦρ ἐν αὐτῷ,
ὑπόκειται δὲ, καὶ ἐκκαίει αὐτοῦ τὰ σπλάγχνα. Οὕτως ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων
πυρέττων τις ἐκκαίεται. Στίχ. κεʹ. Κακώσαι δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπήλυτος τὸν οἶκον. Ὁ
πολεμήσας τὸν λαὸν ἐκεῖνον ἐπήλυτος ἦν, καὶ οὐ προσήλυτος· ὃς ἐκάκωσεν αὐτοῦ
τὸν οἶκον, κατα λύων τὸ νομιζόμενον ἁγίασμα, καὶ τὴν πόλιν ἢν ἔλε γον εἶναι
ἁγίαν. Στίχ. κζʹ. Ἀνακαλύψαι δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ οὐρανὸς τὰς ἀνομίας. Ἀντὶ τοῦ, Καὶ ἐκ Θεοῦ
καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ὑποστή σεται τὰ δεινά. Ταῦτα δὲ ἔφη, ἐπειδὴ ὁ Ἰὼβ, φήσας ὑπὸ Θεοῦ
πεπλῆχθαι, ἐμνημόνευε καὶ ὡς ὑπὸ ἀνθρώ πων ἠδικημένος. Κατασκευάζει οὖν, ὅτι
πάντα δι' ἁμαρτίας αὐτὸν ἐπηνέχθη. Στίχ. κζʹ. Γῆ δὲ ἐπανασταίη αὐτῷ. Αὐτὴ ἡ γῆ
ἐπανίσταται ἐκείνῳ τῷ λαῷ. Στίχ. κθʹ. Καὶ κτῆμα ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ παρὰ τοῦ
ἐπισκόπου. Μανθάνει τίς ἐπίσκοπος ἐνθάδε ὠνομάσθη; ὅτι Θεὸς ἐπίσκοπος εἴρηται,
καὶ οἱ ἐπίσκοποι ἐκεί νου τὴν εἰκόνα παντὶ τῷ τρόπῳ φιλοτιμοῦνται, οἱ καλοὶ καὶ
ἀγαθοὶ, φορεῖν. Καὶ ὥσπερ ὁ μιμησάμενος εἰκόνα βασιλικὴν τιμᾶται ἐπὶ τὸ καλῶς
μιμήσασθαι, τιμᾶται δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ αὐτὴν κεκοσμηκέναι· οὕτως μακάριος ἐπίσκοπος,
ὁ νοήσας τὸν ἀληθινὸν ἐπίσκο πον, καὶ ζηλῶν αὐτὸν, καὶ γινόμενος ὡς ἐν
ἀνθρώποις Θεός· ἢ ἔχων ἐπίσκοπον τὸν ποιοῦντα αὐτὸν ἀληθῶς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ
ἐπίσκοπον· ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κρά τος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν. ΚΕΦ. ΚΑʹ.
Στίχ. εʹ. Εἰσβλέψαντες εἰς ἐμὲ θαῦμα σχέτε. Φατὲ σοφοὶ εἶναι, καὶ εἰδέναι διὰ τί ταῦτα
πά σχω, ὡς τοῦ Θεοῦ μὴ κοιμωμένου ἐπὶ τοῖς ἁμαρ τήμασι τῶν ἀνθρώπων. Καὶ
ἐτολμήσατέ με λέγειν ἁμαρτωλὸν εἶναι, καὶ δικαίως εἰς ταῦτα ἐφθακέναι. Στίχ. ζʹ.
Πεπαλαίωνται δὲ καὶ ἐν πλούτῳ. Οὐκ εἰσὶ νεόπλουτοι, ἀλλὰ πολλὰ ἔτη πεποιή 17.77
κασι πλουτοῦντες, καὶ ἀεὶ τὸν πλοῦτον αὔξοντες. Στίχ. ηʹ. Ὁ σπόρος αὐτῶν κατὰ
ψυχήν. Τοῦ μὲν δικαίου ὁ σπόρος κατὰ πνεῦμά ἐστι· Σπείρει γὰρ εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα, καὶ
ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος θερίζει ζωὴν αἰώνιον· τῶν δὲ τοιούτων, ἐπεὶ ψυχι κὸς ἄνθρωπος
οὐ δέχεται τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος· μω ρία γὰρ αὐτῷ ἐστιν· ὁ σπόρος οὐ κατὰ πνεῦμα,
ἀλλὰ κατὰ ψυχὴν, τὸ ὑποδεέστερον. Στίχ. ηʹ. Τὰ δὲ τέκνα αὐτῶν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς.
Πάντα ὅσα ποιοῦσιν, πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ποιοῦσι. Τέκνα γὰρ τὰ
ἔργα ἑκάστου. Οὐκ ἔστι τέκνα τῶν ἑτεροδόξων ἐν καρδίᾳ, ἐν λογισμοῖς ἀγαθοῖς, ἀλλ'
ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς, πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων. Στίχ. θʹ. Οἱ οἶκοι αὐτῶν
εὐθηνοῦσιν. Ὅτ' ἂν εἰσέλθῃς εἰς συναγωγὴν αἱρετικῶν, καὶ ἴδῃς ἐκεῖ πλῆθος
συναγομένων, βλέπε, ὅτι οἱ οἶκοι αὐτῶν εὐθηνοῦσιν. Στίχ. θʹ. Φόβος δὲ οὐδαμοῦ.
Ἄφοβοί εἰσιν. Οὐ φοβοῦνται τὸν Θεὸν, καταφρο νοῦσι τῆς Θεότητος· τοιαῦτα
λέγοντες περὶ Θεοῦ, οὐ φοβοῦνται, ὅτι περὶ Θεοῦ λαλοῦσιν. Στίχ. θʹ. Μάστιξ δὲ παρὰ
Κυρίου οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπ' αὐτοῖς. Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. Ἐὰν ἴδῃς ἄνθρωπον τοιαῦτα κατὰ Θεοῦ
λαλοῦντα, ὑγιαίνοντα τῷ σώματι, βλέποντα, τὰ αἰσθητήρια σώζοντα, καὶ δοκοῦντα
ἐνίοτε καὶ ἐν τοῖς κοσμικοῖς εὐτυχεῖν· ὅρα, ὅτι πεπλήρωται ἐπ' αὐτοῦ ἀσεβοῦς ὄντος
τό· Μάστιξ δὲ παρὰ Κυρίου οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπ' αὐτοῖς. Στίχ. ιʹ. Ἡ βοῦς αὐτῶν οὐκ
ὠμοτόκησε. Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. Ὁ βοῦς ζῶόν ἐστι γεωργικὸν, καὶ συμπνέων εἰς γεωργίαν.
Καὶ αὐτοὶ γεωργοῦσι. Γεωρ γοῦσι δὲ Σόδομα καὶ Γόμοῤῥα, γεωργοῦσιν Αἴγυπ τον. Ἡ
βοῦς αὐτῶν οὐκ ὠμοτόκησεν· ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπεκύησε, καὶ ἐγέννησε τέκνον, ἵνα
γεωργῆται αὐτῶν ἡ πονηρὰ γῆ. Στίχ. ιʹ. ∆ιεσώθη δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα, καὶ οὐκ
ἔσφηλεν. Ὅσα συλλαμβάνουσι, ταῦτα καὶ κύουσιν, οὐκ ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου Θεοῦ
συλλαμβάνοντες, ἀλλ' ἀπὸ τῆς κα κίας. Ἰδοὺ ὠδίνησεν ἀδικίαν, συνέλαβε πόνον, καὶ
ἔτεκεν ἀνομίαν. Στίχ. ιαʹ. Μένουσι δὲ ὥσπερ πρόβατα αἰώνια. Ποῖος νοῦς ἐστι τοῦ·
μενοῦσιν ὡς πρόβατα αἰώ νια; Περὶ ὧν φησιν ὁ Χριστός· Τὰ ἐμὰ πρόβατα τῆς ἐμῆς
φωνῆς ἀκούουσι, καὶ ἐγὼ ζωὴν αἰώνιον δίδωμι αὐτοῖς, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς· ταῦτά ἐστι τὰ
αἰώνια πρόβατα. Ἐπεὶ οὖν μῖμοί εἰσιν οἱ ἑτερόδοξοι, καὶ ἐθέλουσι μιμεῖσθαι τὴν
pass_a_gloss: Verse 25. And may an arrow go through through his body. These fired arrows wound him. Verse 25. Unburnt fire will eat him down. We learn a certain mystery about the punishment laid up, so that we guard ourselves against suffering it. He said unburnt fire eats down the impious; this fire among us, the material one, is not unburnt fire, for it is seen. But that fire is invisible, the one coming upon the sinners, which burns them within. It is intelligible and punishing. If you want to take an image of that fire, think for me of the one feverish to excess, and being inflamed by fire. You will not find by sight the fire in him, but it lies under and burns out his entrails. Thus someone feverish from the sins is burned out. Verse 25. And may an incomer harm his house. The one having warred against that people was an incomer, and not a proselyte; who harmed his house, dissolving the supposed sanctuary, and the city which they said was holy. Verse 27. And may the heaven uncover his lawlessnesses. Instead of: both from God and from heaven he will undergo the terrible things. And he said these, since Job, having said he had been struck by God, was recalling also how he had been wronged by men. He constructs therefore that all things were brought upon him through sin. Verse 27. And may earth rise up against him. The earth itself rises up against that people. Verse 29. And a possession of belongings for him from the overseer. Learns (read: learn) who is named overseer here? That God is called overseer, and the overseers, the fine and good ones, are ambitious in every way to wear the image of that one. And as the one having imitated a royal image is honoured for imitating it well, and is honoured also for having adorned it; so blessed the overseer, the one having understood the true overseer, and emulating him, and becoming as God among men; or having as overseer the one making him truly overseer in Christ Jesus; to whom the glory and the might into the ages of the ages. Amen. Chapter 21, verse 5. Having looked into me, have wonder. You say you are wise, and know why I suffer these things, as God not sleeping over the sins of men. And you dared to say me to be a sinner, and to have arrived at these justly. Verse 7. And they have grown old also in wealth. They are not newly rich, but have made many years being rich, and always increasing the wealth. Verse 8. Their seed according to soul. Of the righteous the seed is according to spirit; for he sows into the spirit, and from the spirit reaps eternal life; but of such ones, since a soulish man does not receive the things of the spirit, for it is folly to him, the seed is not according to spirit, but according to soul, the inferior thing. Verse 8. And their children in eyes. All that they do, they do toward being seen by men. For children are the works of each. The children of the other-opinioned are not in heart, in good reasonings, but in eyes, toward being seen by men. Verse 9. Their houses prosper. Whenever you enter into a synagogue of heretics, and see there a multitude of those gathered, see that their houses prosper. Verse 9. And fear nowhere. They are fearless. They do not fear God, they despise the Godhead; saying such things about God, they do not fear that they are speaking about God. Verse 9. And a scourge from the Lord is not upon them. Of the same. If you see a man speaking such things against God, healthy in the body, seeing, keeping the sense organs safe, and seeming sometimes also to prosper in worldly things, see that in him, being impious, has been fulfilled the: and a scourge from the Lord is not upon them. Verse 10. Their cow did not give birth untimely. Of the same. The ox is a farming animal, and breathing together toward farming. And they themselves farm. But they farm Sodom and Gomorrah, they farm Egypt. Their cow did not give birth untimely; but she too brought forth, and bore offspring, so that their wicked land is farmed. Verse 10. And their one having in womb was preserved through, and did not slip. As much as they conceive, these they also carry, conceiving not from the fear of God but from the wickedness. Behold he travailed injustice, conceived toil, and bore lawlessness. Verse 11. And they remain like eternal sheep. What is the mind of the: they will remain like eternal sheep? pass_b_english: “And may an arrow pass right through his body” (Job 20:25). These fiery arrows wound him.

“A fire that no one kindled will devour him” (Job 20:26). We are learning a mystery about the punishment that is laid up, so that we may guard against suffering it. He said that an unkindled fire will devour the ungodly man. This material fire that we have is not an unkindled fire, for it is seen. But that fire which comes upon sinners is invisible, and it burns them within. It is a fire of the mind, and it punishes. If you want to take an image of that fire, think, I ask you, of someone with a raging fever, burning as if with fire. You will not find the fire in him by looking; yet it lies beneath and burns up his inward parts. In the same way a person who is feverish from his sins is burned up.

“And may a newcomer ruin his house” (Job 20:26). The one who made war on that people was a newcomer and not a proselyte. He ruined his house, pulling down what was held to be a sanctuary and the city they called holy.

“And may heaven uncover his lawless deeds” (Job 20:27). That is: he will suffer terrible things both from God and from heaven. He said this because Job, after saying that he had been struck by God, also recalled that he had been wronged by men. So he argues that everything was brought upon him through sin. “And may the earth rise up against him” (Job 20:27). The earth itself rises up against that people.

“And a possession of goods is his from the Overseer” (Job 20:29). [Learn] who is named overseer here: God is called Overseer, and the overseers of the Church, the good and noble among them, strive in every way to bear his image. And just as the man who has copied a royal image is honoured for copying it well, and honoured too for having adorned it, so blessed is the overseer who has understood the true Overseer, who is zealous to be like him and becomes as God among men; or who has as his overseer the One who makes him truly an overseer in Christ Jesus. To him be the glory and the power for ever and ever. Amen.

“Look at me and be amazed” (Job 21:5). You claim to be wise and to know why I suffer these things, on the ground that God does not sleep over the sins of men. And you have dared to say that I am a sinner and have come to this justly.
“And they have grown old in wealth” (Job 21:7). They are not newly rich; they have spent many years being rich and always adding to their wealth.

“Their seed is according to the soul” (Job 21:8). The righteous man's seed is according to the spirit: for he sows to the spirit, and “of the spirit reaps eternal life” (Galatians 6:8). But with people of this kind, since “the man of soul does not receive the things of the Spirit, for they are foolishness to him” (1 Corinthians 2:14), the seed is not according to the spirit but according to the soul, the lesser part.

“And their children are before their eyes” (Job 21:8). Everything they do, they do “to be seen by men” (Matthew 23:5). For each person's works are his children. The children of those who hold other doctrines are not in the heart, in good thoughts, but before the eyes, to be seen by men.

“Their houses prosper” (Job 21:9). When you go into an assembly of heretics and see a crowd gathered there, see how their houses prosper. “And there is no fear anywhere” (Job 21:9). They are without fear. They do not fear God; they despise the Godhead. Saying such things about God, they are not afraid, though it is about God that they are speaking. “And there is no scourge from the Lord upon them” (Job 21:9).

From the same: If you see a man saying such things against God who is healthy in body, who sees, who keeps his senses whole, and who at times even seems to do well in the affairs of this world, see how in him, ungodly as he is, the words have been fulfilled: “And there is no scourge from the Lord upon them.”
“Their cow did not cast her calf” (Job 21:10).

From the same: The ox is a farming animal and works together with men at farming. They too farm. But what they farm is Sodom and Gomorrah; they farm Egypt. “Their cow did not cast her calf”: rather, she too brought forth and bore young, so that their wicked land might be farmed.

“And their pregnant one came safely through, and did not miscarry” (Job 21:10). Whatever they conceive, they also carry to term; they do not conceive from the fear of God but from wickedness. “Behold, he travailed with injustice, conceived trouble, and gave birth to lawlessness” (Psalm 7:14).

“And they remain like everlasting sheep” (Job 21:11). What is the meaning of “they will remain like everlasting sheep”? These are the ones of whom Christ says: “My sheep hear my voice, and I give them eternal life” (John 10:27-28), and so on. These are the everlasting sheep.
